title: State-of-the-Art on Model-Informed Drug Development Approaches for Pediatric Rare Diseases

content.abstract_summary: Comprehensive state-of-the-art review of MIDD approaches in pediatric rare disease drug development, illustrating growing regulatory acceptance of pharmacometric modeling in submissions with limited trial data. Six detailed case studies from FDA-approved drugs (risdiplam/SMA, nusinersen/SMA, maribavir/CMV, pozelimab/CHAPLE, mirdametinib/NF1, eteplirsen+delandistrogene/DMD) show how PopPK, PBPK, disease progression models, and exposure-response relationships substitute for traditional RCTs. Future directions include Bayesian trial design, synthetic control arms (including digital twins and generative AI-based approaches), and longitudinal clustering for patient stratification. Authors from Certara, Kura Oncology, Sarepta Therapeutics, Takeda Pharmaceuticals. CPT:PSP 2025.
key_findings: Six regulatory approval case studies: MIDD replaced or supplemented clinical trials in all cases — risdiplam (PBPK for DDI bridging adult→pediatric), maribavir (PopPK simulation of adolescent exposure-matching), pozelimab (single-arm trial + E-R modeling), mirdametinib (PopPK-based pediatric dose selection), eteplirsen and delandistrogene (disease progression + vector load-expression-response analysis)

PBPK + PopPK integration strategy validated in risdiplam: PBPK predicted DDI liability; separate mechanistic PopPK model estimated in vivo FMO3 ontogeny from data across ages 2 months–61 years — enabling a dosing strategy recommendation without additional pediatric DDI trials

Digital twins and synthetic data explicitly listed as 'reduced RCT' approaches: AI/ML-trained virtual control arms, Bayesian hybrid designs, patient-generated health data from wearables — FDA and EMA increasingly accept external controls and real-world evidence for rare diseases

Longitudinal clustering identified as an emerging AI method for rare disease: temporal clustering of disease trajectories identifies patient subgroups missed by cross-sectional analysis; handles irregular visit schedules and missing data common in rare disease registries
MBMA limitations in rare disease: insufficient data, heterogeneous endpoints, limited comparative trials — calls for innovative data sharing and standardization; MIDD fills gaps where MBMA cannot
FDA MIDD paired meeting program: formal pathway to engage agency proactively on MIDD strategy — WG can leverage this as an example of regulatory engagement for AI/pharmacometrics topics

AAV gene therapy (delandistrogene): first application of PK/PD evaluation to AAV-based gene transfer — vector load-expression-response analysis as a new form of MIDD beyond traditional small molecule PK
limitations: Review focuses on regulatory success stories — selection bias toward approved drugs where MIDD worked; failures where MIDD was insufficient are not discussed

AI/ML methods are mentioned only in the forward-looking section (synthetic data, digital twins, clustering) — not yet in the regulatory submission case studies; AI+MIDD is still aspirational not standard practice
MBMA criticism is acknowledged as limited to rare disease context — in common diseases MBMA is well-established; the rare disease limitations do not generalize

extracted_claims.text: Digital twins/simulated control arms: AI/machine learning trained on historical or observational data; model the disease trajectory without intervention for a virtual control arm; no need to withhold treatment from real patients.

Longitudinal clustering represents a transformative approach in pediatric rare disease research, allowing the detection of distinct disease progression phenotypes from complex, temporal clinical data.
Our vision remains that RCTs are replaced by responsible data-integrated alternatives.

numerical_findings.description: Risdiplam PopPK: data from 26 healthy volunteers and 301 SMA patients across infants, adolescents, and adults; weight-based dosing ≤2yr and <20kg, fixed dose ≥2yr >20kg

gaps_addressed: Documents the current regulatory acceptance landscape for MIDD in detail — gives WG a concrete picture of what FDA and EMA already accept and where AI/ML submissions are being positioned

Explicitly bridges AI/ML (digital twins, generative synthetic controls, longitudinal clustering) with the MIDD regulatory framework — provides the connective tissue between what WG is researching and why regulators care
Bayesian hybrid trial designs and external control arms are the pathway through which AI-generated synthetic data enters regulatory submissions — case studies show the regulatory logic chain

provenance.notes: Found via PubMed search 'Bayesian pharmacokinetics regulatory pharmacometrics model informed drug development' (PMID 40697166). Full text retrieved from PMC12625129 (DOI: 10.1002/psp4.70083). CPT:PSP 2025, 14(11):1743-1759. Open access. Authors: industry perspective (Certara, Kura Oncology, Sarepta, Takeda). Full text is 74.8KB — key sections extracted: introduction, case studies summary, Table 1 (selected drugs), Table 2 (synthetic data approaches), future directions (sections 5.4-6.3). The AI/ML section is forward-looking (not yet implemented in submissions) but the regulatory logic chain (MIDD → external controls → synthetic data → digital twins) is well-documented through real approval cases.
